prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 4 "Shipping": indemnified in 1 of 6 earlier cases, t = 0 in 5; when indemnified t per pc about 26 (80% range 19.2 to 39); revealed per pc: 24-27 (case 24)
- line 5 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 8 of 17 earlier cases, t = 0 in 9; when indemnified t per pc about 74 (80% range 45 to 101); revealed per pc: >=68 (case 18*), >=76 (case 21*), >=76 (case 21*), >=76 (case 21*), 34-45 (case 23*), 38-44 (case 25*) (* = other policy wording)
- line 6 "Assembly costs": indemnified in 3 of 4 earlier cases, t = 0 in 1; when indemnified t per pc about 113 (80% range 92 to 151); revealed per pc: >=100 (case 23*), 106-209 (case 24), >=97 (case 24) (* = other policy wording)
- line 7 "Apprentice hours": indemnified in 1 of 4 earlier cases, t = 0 in 3; when indemnified t per hr about 46 (80% range 23 to 145); revealed per hr: 35-36 (case 23*) (* = other policy wording)
- line 8 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 1 of 4 earlier cases, t = 0 in 3; when indemnified t per hr about 39 (80% range 30 to 59); revealed per hr: 35-42 (case 24)
- line 11 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 1 of 4 earlier cases, t = 0 in 3; when indemnified t per hr about 39 (80% range 30 to 59); revealed per hr: 35-42 (case 24)

items.description: Upgrade to premium carbon frame (elective, bicycle recovered undamaged)
items.rationale: Policy 3.1.6, 3.1.7, 7.1.8(b)-(c): The frame swap is an elective upgrade, not caused by the insured event, and the original frame was not damaged. No indemnity.

items.description: Brake replacement as part of routine service
items.rationale: Policy 3.1.6, 7.1.8(a): Routine service and elective replacement, not damage from the theft. No indemnity.
Policy 3.1.6, 7.1.8(a): General servicing and tune-up, not damage from the insured event. No indemnity.
Policy 7.1.7(f), price prior: Shipping is only indemnified if it is necessary to restore an affected item. Here, the bike was not damaged and the shipping relates to elective work. No indemnity.
Policy 7.1.7(g), price prior: Vehicle costs are ancillary and only indemnified if related to covered work. Here, all work is elective or maintenance. No indemnity.
Policy 7.1.7(c), price prior: Assembly is only indemnified if it is part of making good insured damage. Here, it is part of elective upgrade/servicing. No indemnity.
Policy 7.1.7(d), price prior: Labour is only indemnified if it is part of making good insured damage. Here, it is part of elective or maintenance work. No indemnity.
Policy 7.1.7(d), price prior: Labour is only indemnified if it is part of making good insured damage. Here, it is part of elective or maintenance work. No indemnity.

Policy 5.2.2(a), 7.1.7(g): This is a necessary recovery cost for retrieving the stolen bicycle, which is explicitly covered (see reference case 24). Indemnified, but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other recovery costs.

items.description: Cut and remove seized lock to release bicycle
items.rationale: Policy 5.2.2(b): Cutting the lock is a necessary recovery cost for the stolen bicycle, explicitly covered (see reference case 24). Indemnified, but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other recovery costs.

Policy 5.2.2(b), 7.1.7(d): Labour for the lock removal is a necessary recovery cost for the stolen bicycle, explicitly covered (see reference case 24). Indemnified, but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other recovery costs.
